text: The Patriots dominated Pittsburgh 20-3 in their Week 2 home opener at Gillette Stadium, with TreVeyon Henderson scoring a touchdown and the defense absolutely smothering the Steelers in man coverage, though the film breakdown of Drake Maye's performance revealed a QB still searching for the offensive rhythm that fueled last season's Super Bowl run. The victory came at a cost, however: starting right guard Mike Onwenu suffered a broken right ankle that initial X-rays confirmed, dealing another blow to an offensive line already working to gel around their young quarterback. Head Coach Mike Vrabel addressed the injury and the team's Week 2 performance in his Monday press conference, as the Patriots became the first of the original AFL teams to reach 600 wins in franchise history. While the defense's dominance in man coverage masks some of the offensive inconsistencies, Maye will need to find that aggressive-yet-patient balance the coaching staff has emphasized if New England hopes to recapture the championship-caliber play that got them here.
